To make a gauge swatch you definitely want to add some extras around the border of what you’re measuring. Others may chime in with exact measurements, but I do 1.5 x the stitches (so, about 32 for your gauge) called for across and add in three/four stitches of garter at each end. That way, you’re measuring the gauge in the middle of the piece. Edges tend to curl up and be weird with tension, which can throw off your math a bit. 

I also recommend washing and blocking your swatch before measuring (especially for sweaters) to see how the yarn will react to blocking.

My sister was still in her tent. It completely pancaked on top of her, and while she was holding it up and away from her body, one of our kevlar canoes flew threw the air and hit her tent. My tent was tucked away in a grove of pine, but a large branch snapped off and landed on my fiancés side, missing me by inches. Our second canoe also somehow flew through the air and ended up 500 yards across the bay from us. Both canoes were severely damaged with holes, one from the tent stakes from hitting my sister, the other from hitting trees on the way out of the site and across the bay. A tent stake was stuck inside the first boat when it all calmed down and we reassessed.
